248. ### Assertion types
249. 
250. | Type | Description |
251. |------|-------------|
252. | `output_contains` | Agent output contains `value` (case-insensitive) |
253. | `output_not_contains` | Agent output does NOT contain `value` |
254. | `output_matches` | Agent output matches `pattern` (regex) |
255. | `output_not_matches` | Agent output does NOT match `pattern` |
256. | `file_exists` | File matching `path` glob exists in work dir |
257. | `file_not_exists` | No file matching `path` glob exists in work dir |
258. | `file_contains` | File matching `path` glob contains `value` |
259. | `exit_success` | Agent produced non-empty output |
260. 
261. ### Setup options
262. 
263. | Option | Description |
264. |--------|-------------|
265. | `copy_test_files` | When `true`, copies all files from the eval directory (except `eval.yaml`) into the agent working directory before each run. Useful when test fixtures live alongside the eval file. |
266. | `files` | Explicit list of files to create in the working directory. Each entry has a `path` and either inline `content` or a `source` path (relative to the skill directory). Applied after `copy_test_files`. |
267. | `commands` | Shell commands to run in the work directory before the agent starts (e.g. `dotnet build -bl:build.binlog`). |
268. | `additional_required_skills` | List of skill names (from the same plugin) to load in the **isolated** run alongside the target. Useful when an agent routes to specific skills or a skill depends on sibling skills. Does not affect baseline (nothing loaded) or plugin (everything loaded) runs. |
269. | `additional_required_agents` | List of agent names (from the same plugin) to register in the **isolated** run alongside the target. Same semantics as `additional_required_skills` but for agents. |
270. 
271. #### Test fixture files
272. 
273. If a scenario requires files in the agent's working directory (e.g. `.csproj`, `.sln`, `.cs` files), place them alongside `eval.yaml` and opt into auto-copy:
274. 
275. ```text
276. tests/<plugin>/<skill-name>/
277.   eval.yaml
278.   MyProject.csproj
279.   Program.cs
280. ```
281. 
282. ```yaml
283. scenarios:
284.   - name: "Diagnose build failure"
285.     prompt: "Why does this project fail to build?"
286.     setup:
287.       copy_test_files: true    # copies MyProject.csproj, Program.cs into work dir
288.     assertions:
289.       - type: "output_matches"
290.         pattern: "CS\\d{4}"
291. ```
292. 
293. You can also create files inline or reference files from the skill directory:
294. 
295. ```yaml
296. setup:
297.   files:
298.     - path: "input.txt"
299.       content: "inline file content"
300.     - path: "data.csv"
301.       source: "fixtures/sample-data.csv"  # relative to skill directory
302. ```
303. 
304. ### Scenario constraints
305. 
306. Constraints are declarative checks against run metrics — no regex or globs needed:
307. 
308. ```yaml
309. scenarios:
310.   - name: "Test C# scripting"
311.     prompt: "Test stackalloc with nint"
312.     expect_tools: ["bash"]           # agent must use these tools
313.     reject_tools: ["create_file"]    # agent must NOT use these tools
314.     max_turns: 10                    # agent must finish within N turns
315.     max_tokens: 5000                 # agent must use fewer than N tokens
316. ```
317. 
318. | Constraint | Description |
319. |-----------|-------------|
320. | `expect_tools` | List of tool names the agent must use |
321. | `reject_tools` | List of tool names the agent must NOT use |
322. | `max_turns` | Maximum number of agent turns allowed |
323. | `max_tokens` | Maximum token usage allowed |
324. 
325. Constraints are evaluated alongside assertions — a failed constraint means a failed task.
326. 
327. ### Rubric
328. 
329. Rubric items are evaluated by an LLM judge that sees both the baseline and skill-enhanced outputs side-by-side (pairwise mode). The judge determines which output is better per criterion and by how much. Position bias is mitigated by running the comparison twice with swapped order and checking consistency.
330. 
331. In independent mode, rubric items are scored 1–5 per run. Quality metrics have the highest weight (0.70 combined) in the improvement score.
332. 
333. ## Skill profile analysis
334. 
335. Before running the A/B evaluation, skill-validator performs static analysis of each SKILL.md and reports a one-line profile:
336. 
337. ```
338. 📊 crank-benchmarking: 1,722 BPE tokens [chars/4: 2,156] (detailed ✓), 29 sections, 24 code blocks
339.    ⚠  No numbered workflow steps detected
340. ```
341. 
342. This is grounded in [SkillsBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12670) findings (84 tasks, 7,308 trajectories):
343. - **"Detailed" and "compact" skills work best** (+18.8pp and +17.1pp improvement)
344. - **"Comprehensive" skills hurt performance** (–2.9pp) — long documents create cognitive overhead
345. - **Sweet spot is 800–2,500 tokens** (ecosystem median: 1,569 tokens)
346. - **2–3 focused skills outperform 4+** skills bundled together
347. 
348. When a skill fails validation, the profile warnings appear in the diagnosis to suggest what to fix.
349. 
350. ### Getting the token count for a skill

 | `additional_required_agents` | List of agent names (from the same plugin) to register in the **isolated** run alongside the target. Same semantics as `additional_required_skills` but for agents. |
 
 #### Test fixture files
 
 If a scenario requires files in the agent's working directory (e.g. `.csproj`, `.sln`, `.cs` files), place them alongside `eval.yaml` and opt into auto-copy:
 
 ```text
 tests/<plugin>/<skill-name>/
   eval.yaml
   MyProject.csproj
   Program.cs
 ```
 
 ```yaml
 scenarios:
   - name: "Diagnose build failure"
     prompt: "Why does this project fail to build?"
     setup:
       copy_test_files: true    # copies MyProject.csproj, Program.cs into work dir
     assertions:
       - type: "output_matches"
         pattern: "CS\\d{4}"
 ```
 
 You can also create files inline or reference files from the skill directory:
 
 ```yaml
 setup:
   files:
     - path: "input.txt"
       content: "inline file content"
     - path: "data.csv"
       source: "fixtures/sample-data.csv"  # relative to skill directory
 ```
 
 ### Scenario constraints
 
 Constraints are declarative checks against run metrics — no regex or globs needed:
 
 ```yaml
 scenarios:
   - name: "Test C# scripting"
     prompt: "Test stackalloc with nint"
     expect_tools: ["bash"]           # agent must use these tools
     reject_tools: ["create_file"]    # agent must NOT use these tools
     max_turns: 10                    # agent must finish within N turns
     max_tokens: 5000                 # agent must use fewer than N tokens
 ```
 
 | Constraint | Description |
 |-----------|-------------|
 | `expect_tools` | List of tool names the agent must use |
 | `reject_tools` | List of tool names the agent must NOT use |
 | `max_turns` | Maximum number of agent turns allowed |
 | `max_tokens` | Maximum token usage allowed |
 
 Constraints are evaluated alongside assertions — a failed constraint means a failed task.
 
 ### Rubric
 
 Rubric items are evaluated by an LLM judge that sees both the baseline and skill-enhanced outputs side-by-side (pairwise mode). The judge determines which output is better per criterion and by how much. Position bias is mitigated by running the comparison twice with swapped order and checking consistency.
 
 In independent mode, rubric items are scored 1–5 per run. Quality metrics have the highest weight (0.70 combined) in the improvement score.
 
 ## Skill profile analysis
 
 Before running the A/B evaluation, skill-validator performs static analysis of each SKILL.md and reports a one-line profile:
 
 ```
 📊 crank-benchmarking: 1,722 BPE tokens [chars/4: 2,156] (detailed ✓), 29 sections, 24 code blocks
    ⚠  No numbered workflow steps detected
 ```
 
 This is grounded in [SkillsBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12670) findings (84 tasks, 7,308 trajectories):
 - **"Detailed" and "compact" skills work best** (+18.8pp and +17.1pp improvement)
 - **"Comprehensive" skills hurt performance** (–2.9pp) — long documents create cognitive overhead
 - **Sweet spot is 800–2,500 tokens** (ecosystem median: 1,569 tokens)
 - **2–3 focused skills outperform 4+** skills bundled together
 
 When a skill fails validation, the profile warnings appear in the diagnosis to suggest what to fix.

Now I have all the context I need. Here's the answer:

---

## Evaluation Format: `tests/eval.yaml`

Create a `tests/eval.yaml` alongside your skill. Here's an example for a product catalog MCP server:

```yaml
scenarios:
  - name: "Search products by category"
    prompt: "Find all electronics under $50 in the catalog"
    assertions:
      - type: "output_contains"
        value: "electronics"
      - type: "output_matches"
        pattern: "\\$\\d+\\.\\d{2}"
    rubric:
      - "The agent used the catalog search tool rather than guessing"
      - "Results are filtered correctly by category and price"
    reject_tools: ["bash"]
    timeout: 120

  - name: "Product detail lookup"
    prompt: "What are the specifications for product SKU-12345?"
    assertions:
      - type: "output_contains"
        value: "SKU-12345"
    rubric:
      - "The agent retrieved accurate product details from the catalog"
      - "Specifications are presented clearly and completely"
    timeout: 120
```

## What Makes a Good Evaluation Question

**Do:**
- Test things the **baseline model can't answer from training data** (your specific catalog data)
- Use `assertions` for verifiable facts and `rubric` for quality judgment
- Add `setup.files` to give the agent concrete context, reducing variance
- Use `reject_tools: ["bash"]` if the scenario should be pure Q&A (no shell exploration)
- Keep prompts **tight and unambiguous** to reduce run-to-run variance

**Avoid:**
- Questions the model already aces without the skill (no headroom → negative scores from token overhead)
- Overly broad prompts that allow many valid strategies (causes high variance in `perRunScores`)
- Rubrics that enforce one specific approach — accept multiple valid methods

**Key assertion types:** `output_contains`, `output_matches` (regex), `file_exists`, `file_contains`, `output_not_contains`.

See the full spec in the [skill-validator README](https://github.com/dotnet/skills/blob/main/eng/skill-validator/src/README.md) and [Investigating Results](https://github.com/dotnet/skills/blob/main/eng/skill-validator/src/docs/InvestigatingResults.md) for diagnosing failures.
